md_description: This workflow represents Arabidopsis thaliana plants exposed to defined hormone perturbations and environmental stress conditions, followed by transcriptomic RNA-seq and metabolomic LC-MS profiling. The resulting sequencing and mass-spectrometry data are transformed into gene expression and metabolite abundance summaries, then integrated with external reference evidence from prior studies to infer causal links between hormone signaling and stress-response mechanisms. The final output is a dataset-ready metadata-linked causal interaction resource spanning experimental conditions, omics readouts, and literature-supported evidence.

arabidopsis_thaliana_plants.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic identity and origin fields for the living Arabidopsis thaliana specimens before any treatment. I excluded treatment, stress, sequencing, extraction, capture, and derivative-result fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Derivative nodes. I also avoided any sample/experiment identifier fields because root Entity identifiers should be generated once and not repeated elsewhere, and I did not duplicate anything that could overlap with downstream treated-plant or omics nodes.

md_schema.descr: Scientific species name of the living plant material represented by this entity, recorded before any hormone perturbation or stress exposure. Use the canonical binomial nomenclature; for this workflow it should be Arabidopsis thaliana.
Common name for the plant entity, recorded at the time the untreated specimens are defined; typically 'thale cress' or 'Arabidopsis'.
NCBI Taxonomy or equivalent taxonomic identifier for the organism identity, captured once for the entity definition. Example format: '3702' for Arabidopsis thaliana.
Genetic background of the Arabidopsis plants prior to treatment, such as wild-type ecotype or mutant line. Record the exact genotype designation used for the starting material (for example, 'Col-0').
Arabidopsis ecotype or accession designation of the living specimens before any manipulation, if applicable. Example: 'Columbia-0 (Col-0)'.

Developmental stage of the living Arabidopsis plants at the point they enter the workflow, before hormone treatment and stress exposure. Use a controlled vocabulary appropriate to plant development, such as seedling, rosette, bolting, or flowering.

Substrate or cultivation medium on which the plants were originally grown before treatment, such as soil, agar, or hydroponic medium. Record the medium state at the pre-treatment entity stage, not the treatment medium.

High-level cultivation condition of the living plants before hormone perturbation and stress exposure, describing the baseline environment in which the entity existed. Use values that distinguish controlled growth from field-grown material.

hormone_and_stress_treatment.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only protocol and operation fields describing how the hormone perturbation and environmental stress were applied, plus agent/hardware-less execution details relevant to the treatment itself. I excluded plant identity, treated-plant properties, RNA-seq/LC-MS capture settings, and downstream expression/metabolite outputs because those belong to the upstream Entity or downstream Capture/Derivative nodes. I also avoided reusing any sample identifiers and kept the schema focused on the controllable treatment parameters needed to reproduce the perturbation conditions.

md_schema.descr: Plant hormone or hormone class intentionally altered during the treatment step. Record the exact hormone used or perturbed, such as auxin, abscisic acid, salicylic acid, jasmonic acid, ethylene, gibberellin, or cytokinin.

Direction of the hormone perturbation applied to the plants during treatment, relative to baseline or control condition. Indicates whether the hormone was increased, decreased, or held as a control reference.

Applied hormone concentration at the treatment step, expressed in the experiment's working units. Record the final concentration delivered to plants, typically in micromolar or millimolar depending on the hormone and protocol.
Unit used for the applied hormone concentration at the treatment step. Use a controlled value matching the concentration field, such as micromolar or millimolar.

Environmental stress condition applied concurrently with or after hormone perturbation. Record the primary stressor used in this process step, such as drought, salt, cold, heat, osmotic, or oxidative stress.

Magnitude or severity level of the environmental stress imposed during treatment, recorded as a protocol-defined value or category at the moment of exposure. Use the experiment's controlled scale or descriptive level if no numeric scale was used.

Total duration of the hormone and stress exposure, measured from the start of application to the end of the treatment window. Record in minutes; typical values may range from short acute exposures to multi-hour treatments depending on the experiment.

How the hormone perturbation and stress were administered to the plants during this process step. Examples include foliar spray, root drench, medium supplementation, chamber exposure, or combined administration.

Replicate index for this treatment execution, used to distinguish repeated hormone-stress applications under the same nominal conditions. Record as an integer starting at 1 for each treatment condition.

Operational quality indicator for the treatment step, stating whether the intended hormone and stress exposure was successfully completed as planned. Use a simple categorical status to support downstream filtering.

treated_arabidopsis_plants.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing the post-treatment plant material, so I included only intrinsic state fields that describe the treated plants as the sampling substrate: what treatment state they are in, visible/physiological condition after exposure, and whether they are ready for downstream sampling. I excluded the actual treatment protocol parameters, because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded extraction, sequencing, mass-spec, and computed outputs because those belong to downstream nodes. I also avoided identifiers already handled at the root and any fields semantically overlapping with hormone/stress application details.

md_schema.descr: Status of the Arabidopsis plant material after hormone perturbation and stress exposure, describing that this entity is the treated rather than untreated starting material. Use this to distinguish post-treatment material from the pre-treatment plant entity.

Observed condition of the plants immediately after the treatment step and before any downstream sampling or extraction. Record the main qualitative state used by the experimenter, such as healthy, wilted, stressed, damaged, or recovered.

Whether the treated plant material was deemed suitable for downstream RNA extraction or metabolite extraction at the time of entity definition. This is assessed after treatment completion and before sampling begins.

Time elapsed between completion of hormone/stress exposure and the moment the treated plants were sampled or made ready for sampling. Record in minutes; use 0 if sampling occurred immediately after treatment.

Qualitative severity of treatment-associated visible symptoms in the plants, assessed after exposure and before sample collection. Use a controlled category to capture how strongly the treated entity differed from baseline.

rna_extraction_and_library_prep.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only RNA extraction and library preparation protocol fields that describe how treated plant material was converted into an RNA-seq-ready library. I excluded plant-state fields, raw read properties, capture instrument settings, and downstream expression outputs because those belong to the Entity, Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes respectively. I also avoided repeating already_generated treatment fields and kept software/tool names out because this process is a wet-lab preparation step rather than a computational one.

md_schema.descr: Wet-lab method used to isolate RNA from treated Arabidopsis tissue at the start of the transcriptomic preparation workflow. Record the protocol name or extraction chemistry, such as phenol-chloroform, silica column, or magnetic bead-based extraction.

Amount of treated plant material or total RNA input used for RNA extraction and library preparation, measured at the start of this process step. Record the input quantity in the experiment's working unit, typically milligrams of tissue or nanograms of RNA.
Unit used for the RNA or tissue input amount for this preparation step. Choose the unit matching the value recorded in rna_input_amount, such as mg or ng.

RNA integrity metric measured after extraction and before library construction, used to assess whether the RNA quality is sufficient for transcriptomic sequencing. Typical values range from 1 to 10, with higher values indicating better integrity.

Library construction workflow used to convert extracted RNA into sequencing-compatible material, recorded during this process step. Examples include polyA selection, rRNA depletion, or total RNA library preparation.

Key kit or reagent system used for cDNA synthesis and library construction in this preparation step, recorded as the operational preparation chemistry. Example: a named commercial library prep kit or enzyme system.

Number of PCR amplification cycles used during RNA-seq library preparation, measured as part of the wet-lab process. Typical values are protocol-specific and should reflect the actual cycle count used to build the final library.
Fragment size range selected for the final RNA-seq library during preparation, expressed in base pairs. Record the target insert or library size window achieved before sequencing.

Total mass of sequencing-ready library generated at the end of this process step, measured in nanograms. Record the yield of the final prepared RNA-seq library before it is transferred to the sequencing instrument.

rna_seq_library.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing the prepared RNA-seq library itself, so I included only intrinsic library properties and provenance needed to recognize and reuse the prepared material. I excluded extraction and construction protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded sequencing run settings, read file properties, and expression results because those belong to downstream Capture and Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating generic sample identifiers and kept the fields centered on the library as a physical sequencing input.

md_schema.descr: Type of sequencing library represented by this entity, defined here as the prepared nucleic acid library derived from treated Arabidopsis tissue before sequencing. Record the library class used for transcriptomic profiling.

Biological source from which the library was prepared, recorded at the entity level to indicate that the library originated from treated Arabidopsis tissue. Example: treated Arabidopsis leaf tissue or whole-seedling RNA.

Approximate insert size of the prepared RNA-seq library, measured as the fragment length distribution expected at sequencing time. Record in base pairs; typical values depend on the protocol and size-selection window.

Qualitative assessment of whether the prepared library was free of obvious contamination or adapter carryover at the time it was handed off for sequencing. Use a simple status to support downstream filtering.
Storage condition of the prepared RNA-seq library before capture, such as temperature or buffer state, as an intrinsic property of the physical library entity. Example: stored at -20 C in TE buffer.

Measured concentration of the prepared sequencing library at the time it is ready for capture, expressed in ng/µL. Use this to describe the physical library material prior to loading onto the sequencer; typical values depend on the library prep method.

rna_seq_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields for the RNA sequencing run. I described the sequencer hardware identity and actively configured run settings needed to understand how the raw reads were acquired, and I excluded library properties, raw file properties, and downstream alignment/expression outputs because those belong to the Entity, Signal, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any agent name already implied by the node and focused on controllable acquisition parameters at the time of sequencing.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the RNA-seq capture session. Record the hardware vendor for the platform that read the prepared RNA-seq library.
Instrument model used for the RNA-seq sequencing run, recorded at the capture step. Example format: 'NovaSeq 6000' or equivalent platform model.

Serial number or unique hardware identifier of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session. Record the exact device identifier to distinguish instrument-specific run conditions; example format: alphanumeric serial string.

Sequencing chemistry or reagent kit configured on the instrument for this RNA-seq run, such as the read chemistry or flow-cell chemistry used during capture. Record the specific chemistry version if available.
Configured read length for each sequencing read in this capture session, measured in base pairs. Typical values depend on the platform and protocol, such as 50, 75, 100, or 150 bp.
Read layout used by the instrument during the RNA-seq capture session. Indicates whether reads were generated as single-end or paired-end sequences.
Target sequencing depth planned for the run, expressed as millions of reads. Record the intended acquisition depth configured for this capture session, not the final processed read count.

Identifier of the sequencing lane or flow cell used for the capture session. Use this to distinguish separate instrument loading partitions within the same run; example format: lane number or flow-cell barcode.
Date on which the RNA-seq capture session began on the sequencing instrument. Record in ISO date format (YYYY-MM-DD) at the start of acquisition.
Operational status of the sequencing session after completion, indicating whether the instrument run finished successfully and produced usable raw transcriptomic data.

rna_seq_reads.reasoning: I corrected the RNA-seq Signal schema by removing the colliding field read_length_bp because it was already generated elsewhere in the DAG. To stay within Signal territory, I kept only raw artefact properties and technical quality/storage descriptors for the read files, avoiding capture settings and downstream analysis outputs. The remaining fields describe the raw data object itself without duplicating upstream or previously generated metadata.

md_schema.descr: Digital file format of the raw RNA-seq read artefact as stored after sequencing capture. Record the exact format of the reads file, such as FASTQ or BAM, using the representation produced by this workflow.

Total size of the raw read file or files representing this signal, measured in bytes at the time of storage or handoff. Use this to describe the physical data artefact rather than the sequencer output settings.
Total number of sequencing reads contained in the raw RNA-seq signal, counted from the stored file set after capture. Record the observed read total as an integer representing the raw data volume.

Mean base-call quality score across the raw RNA-seq reads, used as a technical quality metric for the stored signal. Typical values are instrument- and run-dependent and are assessed on the raw read artefact rather than after alignment.
Whether adapter sequence contamination was detected in the raw reads at the signal stage. Use this as a simple technical quality flag for the stored read artefact before downstream processing.

Path, URI, accession, or other storage reference where the raw RNA-seq reads are archived. Record the location of the signal file as stored for downstream analysis; example format: file path, object-store URI, or repository accession.
Whether the raw RNA-seq reads are stored in compressed form. Use this to distinguish archived compressed files from uncompressed raw data objects.

read_alignment_and_quantification.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only computational alignment and quantification parameters describing how raw RNA-seq reads were mapped to the Arabidopsis reference and converted into gene-level counts. I excluded raw read properties, library prep details, sequencing capture settings, and the final expression matrix itself because those belong to the Signal, Entity, Capture, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided the previously generated read_length_bp field collision by not repeating any read-size information and focused on workflow/software settings and QC outputs specific to this quantification step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the read aligner used to map RNA-seq reads to the Arabidopsis reference genome during this process step. Example: STAR; record the exact tool used for alignment.
Version of the alignment software used during the read mapping step. Record the exact release or build number to support reproducibility of gene quantification results.
Reference genome assembly version used for RNA-seq alignment and quantification in this process. Example format: TAIR10 or a specific Arabidopsis genome release identifier.
Gene annotation release used to assign aligned reads to Arabidopsis genes during quantification. Record the exact annotation version or release date used at this step.
Software or package used to compute per-gene expression values from the aligned reads. Example: featureCounts; record the exact quantification tool used in this process.

Counting or summarization mode used during quantification, such as gene-level counting, exon-level counting, or transcript-level summarization. Use a controlled category to describe the expression aggregation strategy.

Percentage of raw RNA-seq reads that successfully aligned to the Arabidopsis reference during this process step. Record the mapping rate as a quality indicator for the alignment/quantification workflow, typically as a percentage from 0 to 100.

How reads that aligned to multiple genomic locations were handled during quantification. Use a controlled value to record whether multi-mapped reads were discarded, assigned fractionally, or otherwise processed.

Normalization approach applied during quantification or immediately after count generation within this process step. Record the method used to make per-gene expression values comparable across samples, such as TPM, CPM, or size-factor based normalization.
Operational quality indicator for the alignment and quantification step, indicating whether the workflow completed successfully and produced usable per-gene expression values.

gene_expression_matrix.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result fields that describe the expression matrix itself: how it was generated, its dimensions, normalization/state, and summary quality indicators. I excluded raw read properties, alignment software details, and sequencing/capture settings because those belong upstream to Signal, Process, and Capture nodes. I also avoided any fields already generated earlier in the DAG and kept the schema focused on the reusable matrix artifact that downstream multi-omics integration consumes.

md_schema.descr: Computational method used to produce the gene expression matrix from aligned RNA-seq data, including the primary summarization strategy used for the derived table. Record the exact method or pipeline label used for matrix construction.
Type of numeric values stored in the gene expression matrix, such as raw counts, normalized counts, TPM, or log-transformed abundances. Record the representation actually used in the derived table.

Number of gene features represented as rows in the derived gene expression matrix. Record the matrix dimension after quantification and any filtering, at the point the final expression table is created.
Number of samples or conditions represented as columns in the derived gene expression matrix. Record the final table dimension after sample inclusion and filtering.
Fraction of entries in the derived gene expression matrix that are missing or undefined after computation. Record this as a decimal between 0 and 1 as a summary quality indicator for the final table.

Summary of gene-level filtering criteria applied before or during construction of the derived matrix, such as minimum count thresholds or presence requirements across samples. Record the operational criteria that define which genes remain in the final table.

Whether the gene expression matrix has been normalized, and if so whether normalization was applied before or after matrix construction. Use this to distinguish raw count matrices from processed expression tables.

Digital file format of the derived gene expression matrix as stored for downstream integration, such as CSV, TSV, or HDF5. Record the archive format of the computed artifact rather than the upstream read format.

metabolite_extraction.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only wet-lab extraction protocol fields describing how metabolites were isolated from treated Arabidopsis tissue before LC-MS capture. I excluded plant-state fields, instrument acquisition settings, raw spectra file properties, and downstream abundance tables because those belong to the Entity, Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes respectively. I also avoided repeating RNA-related process fields and focused on solvent composition, extraction conditions, and yield/quality indicators specific to metabolite preparation.

md_schema.descr: Primary solvent or solvent mixture used to extract small-molecule metabolites from treated Arabidopsis tissue during this process step. Record the exact extraction solvent system, such as methanol, acetonitrile, or methanol:water mixtures.

Composition ratio of the solvent mixture used for metabolite extraction, recorded at the time the solvent was prepared for this process step. Example format: 80:20 methanol:water or a similar ratio expression.

Temperature at which the metabolite extraction was performed, measured in degrees Celsius during the extraction step. Typical values may range from chilled extraction conditions to room temperature depending on protocol.

Duration of the solvent-based metabolite extraction, measured from solvent addition to completion of extraction. Record in minutes; typical values are protocol-dependent and may span tens of minutes to hours.

Physical mixing method used during metabolite extraction, such as shaking, vortexing, sonication, or bead beating. Record the primary agitation approach used to improve metabolite recovery from tissue.
Replicate index for the metabolite extraction process, used to distinguish repeated extractions performed under the same nominal conditions. Record as an integer starting at 1 for each condition.

Total amount or relative yield of extracted metabolite material obtained at the end of this process step, measured using the workflow's reporting unit. Record the output quantity as a process-level recovery indicator.
Method used to clarify the metabolite extract before LC-MS capture, such as centrifugation or filtration. Record the primary cleanup step applied after extraction and before instrument analysis.
Operational quality indicator for the metabolite extraction step, indicating whether the extraction completed successfully and produced LC-MS-ready material.

metabolite_extract.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared metabolite extract as a physical sample ready for LC-MS capture. I excluded solvent composition, extraction duration, and other protocol details because those belong to the upstream metabolite_extraction Process node, and I excluded LC-MS settings, spectra files, and derived metabolite tables because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating generic identifiers and focused on sample-specific material properties and readiness for analysis.

md_schema.descr: Primary sample matrix or biological material origin represented by the chemical extract, indicating that the entity comes from treated Arabidopsis tissue prepared for mass spectrometry. Record the source matrix such as leaf extract, whole-seedling extract, or root extract.

Residual solvent system present in the prepared extract entity at the time it is handed off for LC-MS analysis. Record the solvent or solvent mixture that remains associated with the extract, such as methanol:water or acetonitrile-based solvent.

Relative concentration or enrichment level of the prepared metabolite extract prior to LC-MS capture. Use this to describe the sample's concentration state if an absolute concentration was not measured.
Temperature at which the prepared metabolite extract was stored before LC-MS capture, measured in degrees Celsius. Record the storage condition of the entity, such as -80 C, -20 C, or 4 C.

Qualitative stability assessment of the prepared extract at the time it is used for downstream capture. Use a controlled value to indicate whether the extract was considered stable, borderline, or degraded.
Whether the metabolite extract was deemed ready for LC-MS acquisition at the time of entity definition. This indicates sample readiness rather than instrument setup.

lc_ms_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the LC-MS measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields needed to describe how the metabolite extract was acquired. I focused on the LC and MS hardware identity, configured acquisition settings, and run-level status/quality, while excluding sample chemistry, raw spectrum file properties, and downstream metabolite features because those belong to the Entity, Signal, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating any already-generated field names and kept the schema centered on actively controlled acquisition parameters.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the liquid chromatography system used for the LC-MS acquisition session. Record the vendor of the LC module that performed chromatographic separation before mass spectrometry.
Model of the liquid chromatography instrument used during the acquisition step. Example format: a vendor and platform designation for the LC module.
Manufacturer of the mass spectrometer used for this LC-MS capture session. Record the hardware vendor of the MS detector/analyzer system.
Model of the mass spectrometer used during acquisition. Example format: Orbitrap, QTOF, or another specific platform model designation.
Ionization polarity or mode configured for the LC-MS acquisition session. Record whether the instrument operated in positive, negative, or alternate ionization mode for the captured spectra.
Type of chromatographic column configured for separation during LC-MS capture. Record the stationary-phase chemistry or column class used at the instrument session.

Configured mobile phase system used during LC separation in the capture session, including solvent identity and optional additives if recorded by the workflow. Example: water with formic acid / acetonitrile with formic acid.
Total chromatographic gradient length configured for the LC-MS acquisition run, measured in minutes from start to end of the solvent program. Typical values depend on method and column chemistry.
Mass-to-charge acquisition window configured on the mass spectrometer during the capture session. Record the lower and upper m/z bounds used to collect spectra.
Operational status of the LC-MS acquisition session after completion, indicating whether the instrument run produced usable raw spectral data.

lc_ms_spectra.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I kept only raw LC-MS artefact properties and removed the previously colliding generic fields file_format, file_size_bytes, storage_location, and compression_status because they had already been generated for earlier DAG steps. I retained signal-specific dimensions and technical-quality descriptors that are unique to the LC-MS raw spectra and do not overlap with upstream capture settings or downstream metabolite features. I also excluded any instrument configuration, sample chemistry, and derivative interpretation fields because those belong to other node types.

md_schema.descr: Total number of scans or spectra contained in the raw LC-MS signal file, counted from the stored artefact after acquisition. Record the raw data volume as an integer.

Total number of chromatographic data points recorded in the raw LC-MS signal, reflecting the time-resolved measurement density of the stored artefact. Record the observed point count after acquisition.
Mean mass accuracy of the raw LC-MS spectra, expressed in parts per million. Use this as a technical quality indicator for the stored spectral artefact before downstream processing.
Mean signal-to-noise ratio across the raw LC-MS spectra, assessed on the stored signal as a technical quality metric prior to feature extraction.

Digital vendor or exchange format of the raw LC-MS spectral artefact as stored after acquisition. Record the exact spectral file representation used in this workflow, such as mzML or mzXML, using this unique field name rather than the generic file_format label.

Total size of the raw LC-MS spectral file or file set, measured in bytes at the time of storage or archive handoff. Use this to describe the raw data artefact rather than the instrument acquisition settings, with a field name unique to the LC-MS signal node.

Path, URI, accession, or repository reference where the raw LC-MS spectra are archived. Record the location of the signal file set as stored for downstream processing; example format: file path, object-store URI, or repository accession.
Whether the raw LC-MS spectra are stored in compressed form. Use this to distinguish compressed archives from uncompressed raw spectral objects, using a unique field name for this node.

spectral_processing.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only computational processing parameters that transform raw LC-MS spectra into aligned metabolite features and abundance values. I excluded raw spectral file properties, LC-MS acquisition settings, sample extract properties, and the final abundance table itself because those belong to the Signal, Capture, Entity, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided colliding with already generated generic file fields and focused on the peak-picking, alignment, and feature-construction settings that define this processing step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used for peak picking in the LC-MS spectral processing step. Record the exact tool used to detect chromatographic peaks from the raw spectra, such as XCMS or an equivalent package.
Version of the peak-picking software used during spectral processing. Record the exact release or build number to support reproducibility of metabolite feature generation.
Method used to align retention times across LC-MS samples during spectral processing. Record the alignment strategy or algorithm applied to make features comparable across runs.

Mass-to-charge tolerance used when grouping peaks into metabolite features during spectral processing. Record the allowed m/z deviation in the units used by the pipeline, typically as a numeric threshold.

Retention-time tolerance used when grouping aligned peaks into metabolite features during spectral processing. Record the allowed retention-time deviation, typically expressed in seconds or minutes depending on the workflow.
Method used to handle missing peaks across samples during spectral processing, if any. Record how absent feature intensities were treated before the final abundance table was created.
Method used to deconvolute overlapping spectral signals during processing, if applicable. Record the primary deconvolution or feature-resolving approach used before abundance summarization.
Operational quality indicator for the spectral processing step, stating whether peak picking and alignment completed successfully and produced usable metabolite features.
Number of metabolite features detected after peak picking and alignment at the end of this process step. Record the final feature count generated from the raw spectral input.

metabolite_abundance_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-table properties describing the metabolite abundance result itself: generation method, dimensionality, value representation, normalization state, and summary quality indicators. I excluded raw LC-MS artefact fields, capture settings, and processing algorithm details because those belong to Signal, Capture, and Process nodes, and I avoided any already_generated field collisions. The fields are centered on the final reusable metabolite table that downstream integration will consume.

md_schema.descr: Computational method or pipeline used to assemble the derived metabolite abundance table from processed LC-MS features. Record the exact method or workflow label used to create the final table.

Type of numeric values stored in the metabolite abundance table, such as raw intensities, normalized intensities, log-transformed abundances, or relative abundances. Record the representation actually used in the derived table.
Number of metabolite features represented as rows or columns in the derived abundance table, depending on the table layout. Record the final feature count after processing and filtering.
Number of samples or experimental conditions represented in the derived metabolite abundance table. Record the final count included in the table after any filtering or exclusion steps.

Fraction of entries in the derived metabolite abundance table that are missing or undefined after computation. Record this as a decimal between 0 and 1 as a summary quality indicator for the final table.

Summary of feature-level filtering criteria applied before or during construction of the derived abundance table, such as minimum detection frequency or signal threshold requirements. Record the operational rules that determine which metabolites remain in the final table.

Whether the metabolite abundance table has been normalized, and if so whether normalization was applied before or after table construction. Use this to distinguish raw intensity tables from processed abundance tables.

Digital file format of the derived metabolite abundance table as stored for downstream integration, such as CSV, TSV, or HDF5. Record the archive format of the computed artifact rather than the upstream spectral file format.

existing_study_reference_data.reasoning: This node is a Derivative representing externally compiled reference evidence, so I included only fields that describe the evidence set itself: where it came from, what literature/search scope it covers, what kind of evidence it contains, and basic curation/quality summaries. I excluded experimental treatment, capture, signal, and omics result fields because those belong to the wet-lab and derived-data nodes elsewhere in the DAG. I also avoided any fields that would duplicate downstream causal interaction outputs, focusing instead on provenance and content characteristics of the reference evidence resource.

md_schema.descr: Method used to compile the external reference evidence set from prior studies, such as manual curation, database export, or text-mining assisted collection. Record how the evidence resource was assembled.

Scope of the literature or database search used to build the reference evidence set, including organism, hormone, stress, and study type boundaries. Record the breadth of prior studies covered by the compiled evidence resource.

Names of external databases, repositories, or literature sources from which evidence was compiled. Record the source systems used to assemble the reference evidence set, such as curated pathway databases or publication indexes.
Total number of distinct reference items, study records, or evidence statements included in the compiled external evidence set. Record the size of the reference resource as a count.
Primary type of support represented in the compiled evidence set. Use a controlled category to distinguish experimental, observational, computational, or mixed support extracted from prior studies.

Curation status of the compiled reference evidence set, indicating whether the evidence was fully curated, partially curated, or automatically assembled. Record the operational quality state of the reference resource.

Publication year span covered by the external studies included in the reference evidence set. Record the earliest and latest years represented in the compiled resource, for example as a text range such as '2010-2024'.

Summary measure of confidence or support strength across the compiled evidence set, as assessed by the source curation process. Record the overall quality indicator used to prioritize references for downstream inference.

multi_omics_integration.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the integration/inference parameters and operational quality of the computational workflow that combines transcriptomic, metabolomic, and external reference evidence to infer causal interactions. I excluded upstream omics table properties, raw data artefacts, and the final causal interaction dataset fields because those belong to the input Derivative/Signal nodes and the output Derivative node. I also avoided duplicate software fields already used elsewhere unless they are specific to this integration step, and focused on the actual fusion and inference settings needed to reproduce the causal analysis.

md_schema.descr: Name of the computational pipeline or workflow used to integrate transcriptomic, metabolomic, and external reference evidence at this process step. Record the exact integration workflow label used for causal inference.
Version or release of the integration pipeline used to perform the multi-omics causal analysis. Record the exact version identifier to support reproducibility of the inference process.

Source of the transcriptomic input used in the integration step, such as the gene expression matrix or a specific normalized expression table. Record which upstream transcriptomic derivative was consumed by this process.

Source of the metabolomic input used in the integration step, such as the metabolite abundance table or a specific normalized metabolite feature table. Record which upstream metabolomic derivative was consumed by this process.

Source of the external evidence input used in the integration step, identifying the compiled reference evidence set or literature resource consumed by the process. Record which upstream evidence derivative was included in the inference.
Algorithmic method used to infer causal interactions from the combined omics and reference evidence inputs. Record the specific statistical or machine-learning approach used in this process step.

Strategy used to weight transcriptomic, metabolomic, and external reference evidence during integration. Record how different evidence types were combined or prioritized in the causal inference workflow.

Threshold used to retain inferred interactions during the integration process, such as an adjusted p-value cutoff, posterior probability cutoff, or confidence score cutoff. Record the decision threshold applied to the integrated analysis.

Whether the integration process explicitly modeled directed relationships, undirected associations, or mixed interaction types. Use a controlled category to describe the causal orientation assumption used in inference.
Operational quality indicator for the multi-omics integration step, indicating whether the workflow completed successfully and produced a downstream causal dataset.

causal_interaction_dataset.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only fields describing the final computed causal interaction dataset itself: its structure, content types, dimensions, evidence support, and file-level characteristics. I excluded upstream treatment, capture, signal, and integration parameters because those belong to earlier nodes, and I avoided duplicating any already_generated field names or semantically equivalent identifiers. The schema is centered on the final dataset artifact that combines hormone levels, stress conditions, causal interaction calls, and literature-backed evidence for reuse downstream.

md_schema.descr: Computational or curation workflow used to assemble the final causal interaction dataset from the integrated multi-omics analysis. Record the exact method or pipeline label used to produce the dataset artifact.
Number of causal interaction records contained in the final dataset, counted after all integration and filtering steps. Record the size of the derived dataset as an integer.
Number of metadata columns or fields contained in the final causal interaction dataset. Record the final table width after schema assembly.

Summary of the kinds of interactions represented in the final dataset, such as activation, repression, association, or mixed causal links. Record the distribution as a textual summary or encoded categorical summary of interaction classes.

Overall level of literature or reference support attached to causal interaction records in the final dataset. Record how strongly interactions are backed by compiled studies, such as high, medium, or low support.
Summary of the hormone perturbations and environmental stress conditions represented in the final dataset, indicating the scope of experimental scenarios covered by the derived interactions.

Whether the final causal interaction dataset includes normalized quantitative fields, standardized identifiers, or other harmonization steps. Use this to distinguish raw integrated outputs from fully standardized dataset releases.
Digital file format used to store the final causal interaction dataset for downstream reuse, such as CSV, TSV, JSON, or HDF5. Record the archive format of the derived dataset artifact.

Version identifier assigned to the final causal interaction dataset release, used to distinguish successive compiled outputs of the workflow. Record the dataset release version string, for example 'v1.0' or a date-based release tag.

Operational quality indicator for the final causal interaction dataset, indicating whether the compiled resource is complete and suitable for downstream use. Use a simple status summary for the release artifact.
